kind: visual face-identity labels (image evidence only, not physical validation)
labeler: Claude, P1-1 builder, 2026-10-03; one labeler, no second rater
method: Inspected every post-box-*-photo-*.jpg (full crop, dashed 1.1x terminal zooms, unrolled strip between the two associated side lines) plus 2-2.5x zooms of the original photos at mid-height and at both terminals. Computed numbers quoted here come from metrics.json in this directory; the judgements are mine.

vocabulary.B: broad yellow cover plate facing out of the cell toward the approach side (outward face); it does NOT carry the lens window
vocabulary.L: narrower yellow lip plate on the opening side (toward the other curtain); not coplanar with B; shorter than B at both ends
vocabulary.S: dark slot between B and L in which the light-curtain front window (lens strip) is seen; faces the opening
vocabulary.E_post: outer vertical edge of B on the white post / fence side
vocabulary.E_junction: B/L junction = B's opening-side edge = edge of the slot S

faceClass.outward_cover_plate_only: the two side lines bound B alone
faceClass.outer_silhouette_spanning_two_faces: the two side lines are E_post and E_lip, so the bounded region contains B, L (and S where visible)

housingCrossSection.summary: Not a flat bar. Both curtains (mirror images) sit in a stepped two-plate yellow guard: broad outward cover plate B plus a narrower lip plate L on the opening side, meeting at an angle, with the dark light-curtain front window recessed in the slot S between them and facing across the entrance. L ends lower at the top (~7-17 raw px in the image) and higher at the bottom (~30-45 raw px; measured 30-44 px from yellow-extent profiles in p1/p3/p4 right and p2 left) than B. Black bracket at the top on the post side, earth bolt at B's bottom, yellow clips on both plates.
housingCrossSection.evidenceNotCoplanar: Apparent L/B width ratio changes with viewpoint (right curtain 0.63 p1, 0.60 p3, 0.45 p4, L invisible p2; left curtain 0.14 p1, 0.63 p2, 0.13 p3, ~0.24 p4, read from the unrolled-strip yellow/value profiles in metrics.json). Two coplanar parts would keep a nearly constant ratio for these camera positions; L also changes shade relative to B (darker in p1/p3/p4 for the right curtain).
housingCrossSection.evidenceSlotIsLensSide: S is visible only from the views that look at the opening side: photo 1 for the right curtain (camera left of it), photo 2 for the left curtain (camera far right). In photo 1 it shows a fine-textured dark strip consistent with a light-curtain front window; it is hidden or closed to a seam elsewhere.
housingCrossSection.roughOrientationCheck: Left curtain: B alone is 104 px wide in photo 1 and ~59 px in photo 2 (ratio 1.76). If B had the fitted face orientation the ratio would be ~1.1; ~1.8 corresponds to B facing roughly 45 deg further toward the cameras than the fitted plane. The fitted left face therefore lies between B and L, as a plane through E_post and E_lip of two different faces would. Horizontal-only approximation, +-10 deg.
